steps.heading: From your documents to a first draft
steps.intro: Setup takes about five minutes once you're in, and the app walks you through each part.

items.title: Upload what you already know
items.body: Policies, product guides, meeting notes. Your agents answer from them and name the file they used.

items.title: Give it a job and a time
items.body: Pick one of eight roles and when it works: every Monday at nine, every Friday, or the moment a customer writes.

items.title: Read it over coffee
items.body: The work is done and waiting in one inbox. Approve it, edit it, or bin it. A weekly digest sums up the rest.

features.heading: One morning's output, before you start
features.intro: One morning at ABC Inc.: what's done, and what's waiting on you.

items.label: Approvals inbox
items.title: Nothing goes out until you say so
items.body: Every post, email and ticket waits here with its full text. Approve, edit or reject in one click. Every decision is logged.

items.label: Nova · Marketer
items.title: Monday's post, written on Sunday night
items.body: Nova reads what changed this week and drafts the post in your voice. You approve it before anyone sees it.

items.label: Mia · Support
items.title: The warranty question, answered at 2am
items.body: Mia answers from the returns policy you uploaded and names the file. When it isn't in there, she hands it to you.

items.label: Sol · Researcher
items.title: What three competitors did this week
items.body: Sol runs your standing question every Friday and writes it up with numbered sources you can open and check.

items.label: Leo · Sales rep
items.title: Five new leads, each with a reason
items.body: Leo finds businesses that fit your ideal customer and drafts a first email to each. They wait for your approval.

items.label: Kai · Assistant
items.title: The follow-up that didn't slip
items.body: Kai drafts the email from your meeting notes and proposes the next date. It sends when you confirm.

trust.heading: It asks before it acts
trust.intro: Handing work to an AI is a bigger ask than trying another app. So an agent drafts, and a person decides.

shots.title: Every email and post waits with its full text
shots.body: Every email, post, calendar event and Slack message waits with its full text. Approve, edit or reject.

shots.title: It can, it can't - on every agent
shots.body: Each agent's page says exactly what it does on its own and what it never does without you.

shots.title: Hand-offs you can follow
shots.body: When one agent asks another for help, the whole exchange is one thread in the Audit log.

items.title: Draft-only by default
items.body: A new agent cannot publish or send anything. You allow that yourself, per agent and per tool.

items.title: You approve every send
items.body: Posts and emails wait in your inbox with the full text. Approve, edit or reject — from your phone.

items.title: Answers name their source
items.body: Agents answer from your documents and cited web pages. When the answer isn't there, they say so.

items.title: A full audit log
items.body: Every run, draft and decision is recorded: who did what, and when.

items.title: Your documents are yours
items.body: Nothing you upload is used to train an AI model. Saved credentials are encrypted.

items.title: It knows when to stop
items.body: Each agent has a rule for handing off. When it applies, the agent stops and brings in a person.

roles.heading: Eight roles, ready to hire
roles.intro: Pick one and change anything: its job, its voice, the documents it reads, when it asks you.

items.q: What can an agent actually do?
items.a: It answers your clients on a chat link or a widget on your site, searches the documents you upload, researches the web with citations, drafts posts and emails, logs bugs and requests, and schedules its own follow-ups. It can work on a schedule or the moment someone writes in.

items.q: Will it ever send something I haven't seen?
items.a: No. Every agent starts in draft-only mode, so posts and emails wait for your approval in the Inbox. You can loosen that per agent and per tool once one has earned it.

items.q: What happens if an agent gets it wrong?
items.a: You catch it in the inbox, because the draft is the thing you approve: reject it, or edit it and send the version you want. Every agent also has an escalation rule that stops it and brings in a person, and the audit log shows what it did and which sources it used.

items.q: Where do its answers come from?
items.a: From the documents you upload (PDF, Word, Markdown, text) and from cited web pages. When the answer is in neither, the agent says it doesn't know rather than inventing one.

Nothing you upload is used to train an AI model, and your documents are readable only inside your organisation. Integration credentials such as API keys are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. It is stored with our hosting and database providers, Vercel and Neon, and deleted when you close your organisation.

items.q: Can I connect my own tools?
items.a: Today an agent can send email through your own Resend account, post notifications to Slack or any webhook, take work in through an inbound webhook, and talk to clients through a hosted link or the embed widget. Direct Gmail, LinkedIn and Slack posting are not built yet.
About five minutes: pick a role, upload a document, test it live in the playground, publish. The app has a step-by-step guide for each part, from hiring an agent to reading the audit log.

items.q: What languages does it work in?
items.a: An agent reads your documents and replies in the language you write its job in, and the models behind it handle the major languages well. The Desker interface itself is English only today.
